'''Philipp Kukura''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] (born 26 March 1978) is Professor of [[Chemistry]] at the [[University of Oxford]], and a Fellow of [[Exeter College, Oxford]].<ref name="CVI">{{Cite web | url = http://kukura.chem.ox.ac.uk/Data/Sites/51/cvkukura_forwebsite2.pdf | title = Curriculum Vitae | last = Kukura | first = Philipp | publisher =  | date =  | access-date = 17 March 2021 | archive-date = 21 March 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210321115408/http://kukura.chem.ox.ac.uk/Data/Sites/51/cvkukura_forwebsite2.pdf | url-status = dead }}</ref> He is best known for pioneering contributions to femtosecond stimulated Raman spectroscopy (FSRS), [[interferometric scattering microscopy]] (iSCAT) and the development of mass photometry.
 
==Education and early life==
He was born in [[Bratislava]], then [[Czechoslovakia]]<ref name=EOA>{{Cite web|url=https://www.exeter.ox.ac.uk/people/professor-philipp-kukura/|title=Professor Philipp Kukura|website=Exeter College}}</ref> in a family of Slovak actor [[Juraj Kukura]]. In 1984, the family emigrated to Germany.{{cn|date=September 2026}} In 2002, he graduated with a [[Master of Chemistry]] from the [[University of Oxford]] and competed in the 2001 and 2002 Rugby League Varsity matches. In 2006, he completed his PhD in Chemistry from the [[UC Berkeley College of Chemistry|University of California, Berkeley College of Chemistry]].{{cn|date=September 2026}}

==Career and research==
After completing his PhD, Kukura moved to [[Zürich]]. There he worked at the [[ETH Zurich|Swiss Federal Institute of Technology]] as a postdoctoral research assistant under the supervision of Professor Vahid Sandoghdar on [[Nanophotonics|nano-optics]] until 2010.<ref name=EOA/> He returned to Oxford in 2010 to work initially as an EPSRC Career Acceleration Fellow. In 2011, he was elected to a tutorial fellowship at Exeter College.<ref name=EOA/> In 2016 he was promoted to Full Professor of Chemistry.<ref name="CVI"/>  

In 2018, Kukura founded Refeyn Ltd. together with Justin Benesch, Daniel Cole, and Gavin Young to commercialise [[mass photometry]].<ref name="CVI"/>
